pr_title: kvserver: tighten and de-fatal replicaGC checks
pr_body:
Now we return most failed checks as errors and report errors to sentry (but
without crashing).

Closes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/94813.

Epic: None
Release note: None

comments:
I don't immediately see how this can happen, one should not be able to hit this path.

In `replicaGCQueue.process`, we already hold a reference to a `*Replica`, whose replicaID ought to never change:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9f47a214c41e14af661a07600c66ddcdbf525bbc/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_gc_queue.go#L217-L218

We then query meta2, and in this case evidently determined to go ahead with replicaGC which implies `!sameRange && !currentMember`:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9f47a214c41e14af661a07600c66ddcdbf525bbc/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_gc_queue.go#L250-L251

where we're comparing to a consistent read of the meta2 copy of the range descriptor. The `nextReplicaID` in this case is `4` and our replica should really have `3` or less. We could be checking that right there in the queue, but for some reason don't. (We should add it).

As is, the assertion might have been triggered by data loss on the meta2 range (or any other reason why the consistent read returned an incorrect result). Or the replica was removed and immediately re-added, and somehow the replica was replaced in-place. This would be quite surprising, actually is basically impossible, since we assign to `replicaID` in only one place, a place that returns a fresh `*Replica`.

I think we should tighten up the replicaGC processing with additional sanity checks and call it a day.

The original sentry report has expired, so there's no additional information available (such as whether the cluster had other issues).
